question.problem: The vector $a$ is directed due north-west and $|\,a\,|=5$, while the vector $b$ is directed due south-west and $|\,b\,|=12.$ Which of the following is a unit vector that is parallel to $a+b?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we have to find $a+b.$ According to the triangle law of addition, the resultant $a+b$ goes from the tail of $a$ to the head of $b:$   

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14251721/assets/153aff405a3ae0859ff74fcb98deb09e038db7b033cbe54223866c9fe1724fb1.png)

To find the unit vector corresponding to $a+b,$ we have to divide by the magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{a+b}{|a+b|}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the magnitude, first notice that we obtain a right triangle. So, we can use the Pythagorean theorem:

$$
\begin{aligned}{|a+b|}^{2} & ={|a|}^{2}+{|b|}^{2} \\  & ={5}^{2}+{12}^{2} \\  & =169\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the magnitude is

$$
|a+b|=\sqrt{169}=13,
$$

and the corresponding unit vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{a+b}{|a+b|} \\  & =\frac{1}{13}(a+b).\end{aligned}
$$
